h2. OCPBUGS draft

*Title:* {{nmstate-configuration.sh}} SHA idempotency check never runs due to invalid {{[}} test syntax

*Component:* {{machine-config-operator}}  
*Affects:* OpenShift *4.20* and later (MCO {{release-4.20+}}). *Not* present on 4.16–4.19 (those branches still use {{if [ -e …/applied ]; then exit 0}}).

*Description*

{{nmstate-configuration.sh}} (Ignition template {{templates/common/_base/files/nmstate-configuration.yaml}}) is meant to skip work when the config under {{/etc/nmstate/openshift/}} is unchanged by comparing SHA256 of {{applied}} to the selected host/cluster YAML.

Since commit {{94da375b3}} (“Add improved check for already applied configs in nmstate-configuration.sh”, 2025-06-18), the comparison uses invalid test syntax:

{code:bash}if ["$sha_applied"=="$sha_config"]; then{code}

There must be a space after {{[}} and before {{]}} for {{[}} to invoke {{test}}. After variable expansion bash tries to run a command literally named {{[<sha>==<sha>]}}, which fails with “command not found”.

Because the failure occurs in the {{if}} condition, {{set -e}} does *not* stop the script. The early-exit branch is never taken; the script always continues to {{ovs-vsctl --if-exists del-br br-ex}} / {{br0}} and re-copies the config on every service run whenever {{/etc/nmstate/openshift/applied}} already exists.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Use a cluster on OCP 4.20+ with NMState config delivered via MCO ({{/etc/nmstate/openshift/cluster.yml}} or per-host YAML).
# Boot once so {{nmstate-configuration.service}} creates {{/etc/nmstate/openshift/applied}}.
# Reboot or restart the unit:  
{{systemctl restart nmstate-configuration.service}}
# Inspect logs (script uses {{set -eux}}):  
{{journalctl -u nmstate-configuration.service -b}}

*Actual results*

* Log line similar to: {{[<sha256>==<sha256>]: command not found}}
* No “Configuration already applied, exiting”
* {{ovs-vsctl … del-br br-ex}} (and related steps) run again even when config is unchanged

*Expected results*

* When {{applied}} matches the current config (same SHA or same file content), the script prints “Configuration already applied, exiting” and exits 0 without deleting bridges or re-copying.

*Impact*

* Idempotency / “already applied” optimization broken on every node after first successful run.
* Extra OVS bridge teardown attempts on each boot (usually {{--if-exists}}, but unnecessary and noisy).
* Misleading errors in journal; harder to debug real NMState/OVS issues.
* Config *changes* may still be applied because the script falls through on the failed {{if}}, masking the fact that the “unchanged → skip” path never worked.

*Root cause*

Typo: missing spaces in {{[}} / {{]}} test expression (ShellCheck SC1035 / SC1020).

*Suggested fix*

{code:bash}if [ "$sha_applied" = "$sha_config" ]; then{code}

(or {{[[ "$sha_applied" == "$sha_config" ]]}}; script is {{#!/bin/bash}}).

Optional hardening: compare files with {{cmp -s "$src_path/applied" "$src_path/$config_file"}} since {{applied}} is a copy of the config.

*References*

* MCO template: {{machine-config-operator/templates/common/_base/files/nmstate-configuration.yaml}} (approx. line 32)
* Introduced: {{94da375b3}}; present on {{origin/release-4.20}} and newer release branches; absent on {{release-4.19}} and earlier

{{nmstate-configuration.sh}} (Ignition template {{templates/common/_base/files/nmstate-configuration.yaml}}) is meant to skip work when the config under {{/etc/nmstate/openshift/}} is unchanged by comparing SHA256 of {{applied}} to the selected host/cluster YAML.

Since commit {{94da375b3}} (“Add improved check for already applied configs in nmstate-configuration.sh”, 2025-06-18), the comparison uses invalid test syntax:

{code:bash}if ["$sha_applied"=="$sha_config"]; then{code}

There must be a space after {{[}} and before {{]}} for {{[}} to invoke {{test}}. After variable expansion bash tries to run a command literally named {{[<sha>==<sha>]}}, which fails with “command not found”.

Because the failure occurs in the {{if}} condition, {{set -e}} does *not* stop the script. The early-exit branch is never taken; the script always continues to {{ovs-vsctl --if-exists del-br br-ex}} / {{br0}} and re-copies the config on every service run whenever {{/etc/nmstate/openshift/applied}} already exists.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Use a cluster on OCP 4.20+ with NMState config delivered via MCO ({{/etc/nmstate/openshift/cluster.yml}} or per-host YAML).
# Boot once so {{nmstate-configuration.service}} creates {{/etc/nmstate/openshift/applied}}.
# Reboot or restart the unit:  
{{systemctl restart nmstate-configuration.service}}
# Inspect logs (script uses {{set -eux}}):  
{{journalctl -u nmstate-configuration.service -b}}

*Actual results*

* Log line similar to: {{[<sha256>==<sha256>]: command not found}}
* No “Configuration already applied, exiting”
* {{ovs-vsctl … del-br br-ex}} (and related steps) run again even when config is unchanged

*Expected results*

* When {{applied}} matches the current config (same SHA or same file content), the script prints “Configuration already applied, exiting” and exits 0 without deleting bridges or re-copying.

*Impact*

* Idempotency / “already applied” optimization broken on every node after first successful run.
* Extra OVS bridge teardown attempts on each boot (usually {{--if-exists}}, but unnecessary and noisy).
* Misleading errors in journal; harder to debug real NMState/OVS issues.
* Config *changes* may still be applied because the script falls through on the failed {{if}}, masking the fact that the “unchanged → skip” path never worked.

*Root cause*

Typo: missing spaces in {{[}} / {{]}} test expression (ShellCheck SC1035 / SC1020).

*Suggested fix*

{code:bash}if [ "$sha_applied" = "$sha_config" ]; then{code}

(or {{[[ "$sha_applied" == "$sha_config" ]]}}; script is {{#!/bin/bash}}).

Optional hardening: compare files with {{cmp -s "$src_path/applied" "$src_path/$config_file"}} since {{applied}} is a copy of the config.

*References*

* MCO template: {{machine-config-operator/templates/common/_base/files/nmstate-configuration.yaml}} (approx. line 32)
* Introduced: {{94da375b3}}; present on {{origin/release-4.20}} and newer release branches; absent on {{release-4.19}} and earlier

items.toString: KMS Key Rotation Fails - First rotation succeed, second fails [release-4.22]

Previously, KMS key rotation could fail on the second rotation because the KAS deployment convergence check did not account for terminating pods. Kubernetes deployment status fields exclude terminating pods, so the convergence check returned true while old KAS pods with stale encryption configs were still running. This caused premature state advancement in the rotation state machine, leading to encryption config mismatches and KAS pods failing with 'no matching prefix found' errors. With this fix, the convergence check now verifies that no terminating pods exist before reporting the KAS deployment as converged, ensuring each rotation phase completes cleanly before advancing.

items.fromString:
*Description of problem:*

{noformat}The cluster-network-operator (CNO) fails to reconcile the mtu-prober Job in the guest cluster when the desired spec.template differs from the existing Job. Since Kubernetes Job spec.template is immutable after creation, the CNO's apply/update operation fails permanently. The CNO does not implement delete-and-recreate fallback logic, resulting in an unrecoverable deadlock that blocks the entire cluster installation.{noformat}

*Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):*

{noformat}4.20{noformat}

*How reproducible:*

{noformat}100% given the reproducible steps followed carefully{noformat}

*Steps to Reproduce:*

{noformat}1. Create an HCP KubeVirt HostedCluster (OCP 4.20.x)
2. Allow the initial CNO to create the mtu-prober Job in the guest cluster's openshift-network-operator namespace
3. Modify the proxy configuration on the HostedCluster CR (add/change HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY), OR allow the CNO pod to restart with updated environment
4. Observe that the CNO enters a permanent error loop attempting to update the existing mtu-prober Job{noformat}

*Actual results:*

{noformat}The CNO continuously fails with:

mtu_probe.go:104] Could not apply mtu-prober object: failed to apply / update 
(batch/v1, Kind=Job) openshift-network-operator/mtu-prober: Job.batch "mtu-prober" 
is invalid: spec.template: Invalid value: [...]: field is immutable{noformat}

*Expected results:*

{noformat}When the CNO encounters a "field is immutable" error on the mtu-prober Job, it should:
- Delete the existing stale Job
- Recreate the Job with the correct/current spec
- Continue the MTU probe flow normally{noformat}

*Impact cascade:*

* MTU probe never completes → CNO cannot determine network MTU
* CNO does not render OVN-Kubernetes manifests
* No pods deploy in {{openshift-ovn-kubernetes}} namespace
* All guest cluster nodes remain {{NotReady}} (no CNI)
* Cluster installation is permanently blocked
* Multiple ClusterOperators remain unavailable (network, dns, ingress, monitoring, etc.)
* Manual deletion of the Job does not self-heal (CNO does not recreate it — see Additional Notes)



*Additional info:*

{noformat}In pkg/network/mtu_probe.go (line ~104), the CNO uses server-side apply to manage the mtu-prober Job. When the apply fails due to spec.template immutability, the error is logged but no recovery action is taken. The reconciliation simply returns the error and retries with exponential backoff — hitting the same immutable field error every time.

The spec.template changes because the CNO injects environment variables (proxy settings, KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST/PORT) into the Job's pod template at reconciliation time. If these values change after the Job was first created, the apply is permanently broken.

Fix should be:

when the apply/update returns an IsInvalid error with "field is immutable", the CNO should delete the existing Job and retry creation:{noformat}

Fix should be:

when the apply/update returns an IsInvalid error with "field is immutable", the CNO should delete the existing Job and retry creation:{noformat}

items.fromString:
h2. Summary

When ACM addon-uninstall pods ({{addon-config-policy-controller}}, {{addon-governance-policy-framework}}) are evicted due to MemoryPressure on infra nodes, ACM never retries them. This causes HCP cluster deletion to hang permanently on klusterlet/addon finalizers.

h2. Root cause

During the ARO HCP stage e2e capacity exhaustion incident (AROSLSRE-1373), Prometheus on infra nodes consumed excessive memory, triggering MemoryPressure evictions. The evicted addon-uninstall pods were never recreated by ACM, leaving clusters stuck in a deleting state indefinitely.

As noted in the incident analysis: "the bug here is not the eviction, it's that ACM does not re-try." Eviction is a normal Kubernetes behavior; the controller should handle it gracefully by retrying the uninstall job.

h2. Impact

* ~22 stale hosted control planes accumulated on the stage management cluster
* The same MemoryPressure pattern was observed in prod regions (uksouth, canadacentral, brazilsouth, centralindia)
* Any future memory pressure event on infra nodes will cause the same deletion hang

h2. Expected behavior

When addon-uninstall pods are evicted (for any reason), ACM should detect the eviction and recreate the pods to complete the uninstall process.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Have a management cluster with HCP clusters managed by ACM
# Cause MemoryPressure on infra nodes (e.g., Prometheus consuming excessive memory)
# Observe addon-uninstall pods being evicted
# Attempt to delete an HCP cluster
# Observe deletion hangs on klusterlet/addon finalizers because uninstall pods are never retried

h2. Related

* AROSLSRE-1373 (umbrella incident)
* AROSLSRE-1428 (ACM pods evicted by Prometheus memory pressure)
* AROSLSRE-1377 (deletion stuck on klusterlet/addon finalizers)
* openshift/hypershift#8804 (related HyperShift PR)

h2. Summary

When ACM-managed pods are evicted (for any reason — MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, etc.), ACM does not detect the eviction and recreate the pods. This affects all ACM-deployed pods — not only addon-uninstall pods, but also registration agents and other components. When eviction happens during cluster deletion, the ManagedCluster CR gets permanently stuck because addon cleanup never completes, which in turn blocks ARO HCP from removing the HostedCluster (ManagedCluster CR removal is a prerequisite for HostedCluster deletion).

h2. Root cause

ACM deploys pods for addon lifecycle management (install, uninstall) and cluster registration. When these pods are evicted by the kubelet due to node pressure conditions, ACM's controllers do not reconcile the missing pods. The evicted pods remain in {{Failed}} status and are never replaced, leaving finalizers on ManagedCluster and ManagedClusterAddon resources that block deletion indefinitely.

This is not specific to uninstall pods — any ACM-deployed pod (registration agent, policy controllers, etc.) that gets evicted will not be retried.

h2. Impact

* ~22 stale ManagedCluster CRs accumulated on the ARO HCP stage management cluster, preventing removal of the corresponding HostedCluster resources and exhausting scheduling capacity
* The same pattern was observed in prod regions (brazilsouth, uksouth, canadacentral, centralindia) with DiskPressure and MemoryPressure evictions
* Any future node pressure event on nodes running ACM pods will cause the same hang
* Stuck ManagedCluster CRs hold up the entire deletion chain: ManagedCluster CR removal is a prerequisite for HostedCluster deletion in the ARO HCP architecture

h2. Expected behavior

When any ACM-deployed pod is evicted (for any reason), ACM should detect the eviction and recreate the pod to maintain the desired state. This applies to all ACM pod types: registration agents, addon controllers, uninstall jobs, policy framework pods, etc.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Have a management cluster with HCP clusters managed by ACM
# Cause node pressure (MemoryPressure or DiskPressure) on nodes running ACM pods
# Observe ACM pods being evicted
# Attempt to delete an HCP cluster
# Observe ManagedCluster CR deletion hangs on {{managedclusteraddons}} finalizer because uninstall pods are never retried
# The stuck ManagedCluster CR prevents the HostedCluster from being removed

h2. Related

* AROSLSRE-1373 (umbrella incident — stage capacity exhaustion)
* AROSLSRE-1428 (ACM pods evicted by Prometheus memory pressure)
* AROSLSRE-1377 (deletion stuck on klusterlet/addon finalizers)

h2. Summary

Since the merge of [openshift/cluster-ingress-operator#1484|https://github.com/openshift/cluster-ingress-operator/pull/1484] (NE-2664: deploy haproxy as sidecar) on 2026-07-01, Azure TechPreview IPI installations consistently fail with a 45-minute bootstrap timeout. The failure rate is 100% — 3 consecutive failures since Jul 2, all with the same root cause.

h2. Root Cause

The router container's startup probe checks {{/healthz/ready}} which requires both {{has-synced}} and {{backend-http}} to pass. During bootstrap, the Route API ({{routes.route.openshift.io}}) is not yet available because {{openshift-apiserver}} hasn't registered it. The router can't sync routes, so the startup probe kills the container every ~120 seconds, creating a restart loop.

_Failure chain:_

h1. {{openshift-apiserver}} not ready → Route API ({{routes.route.openshift.io}}) not registered

h1. Router container can't list/watch Routes: {{failed to list *v1.Route: the server could not find the requested resource}}

h1. {{/healthz/ready}} returns HTTP 500 ({{has-synced}} and {{backend-http}} fail, only {{process-running}} passes)

h1. Startup probe kills router every 120s ({{failureThreshold=120 × periodSeconds=1}})

h1. 11 restarts, 1,314 startup probe errors

h1. Ingress operator reports {{Available=False}} ({{DeploymentUnavailable: MinimumReplicasUnavailable}})

h1. Monitoring can't create Routes → {{the server could not find the requested resource (post routes.route.openshift.io)}}

h1. Authentication: oauth-server endpoints not ready

h1. 45-minute bootstrap timeout exceeded

h2. What PR #1484 Changed

||Before|| ||After||
|1 container (router with embedded HAProxy)|3 containers: init-router → haproxy sidecar → router|
|Router resources: 100m CPU / 256Mi|Router resources: _25m CPU / 64Mi_|
|Pod starts immediately|init-router copies config → haproxy sidecar must pass 120s startup probe → then router starts|

_Note:_ The sidecar deployment is _unconditional_ — it's not gated behind a feature gate. TechPreview clusters are hit first because they have more operators/CRDs competing for resources during bootstrap, but non-TechPreview may follow if provisioning is slow.
